OG Anunoby Jr. was born on 17 July 1997.
OG Anunoby Jr.'s birthplace is London, England.
OG Anunoby's father taught as a professor in England at the time of his son's birth.
OG Anunoby's mother died of cancer when he was one year old.
OG Anunoby moved to the U.S. with his family at the age of four.
OG Anunoby's father is named Ogugua Sr.
OG Anunoby has an older brother named Chigbo.
Chigbo played in the NFL for the Cleveland Browns, Tennessee Titans, and Minnesota Vikings before entering medical school.
OG Anunoby played football when he was young but stopped around age eight to focus on basketball due to his height.
OG Anunoby played high school basketball at Jefferson City High School.
During OG Anunoby's senior season in high school, he averaged 19.1 points and 8.6 rebounds per game.
OG Anunoby was named a finalist for Mr Basketball in the state of Missouri during his senior year.
OG Anunoby chose to attend Indiana University over Georgia, Iowa, George Mason, and Ole Miss in October 2014.
In 2015–16 at Indiana, OG Anunoby appeared in 34 games as a freshman.
As a freshman in the 2015–16 season, OG Anunoby averaged 6.9 points, 6.6 rebounds, and 0.6 assists per game.
OG Anunoby injured his right knee against Penn State on 18 January 2017 during his sophomore year at Indiana.
OG Anunoby underwent season-ending knee surgery after injuring his right knee in January 2017.
On 10 April 2017, OG Anunoby declared his intention to enter the 2017 NBA draft and hire an agent.
On 22 June 2017, OG Anunoby was selected with the 23rd overall pick in the 2017 NBA draft by the Toronto Raptors.
On 9 July 2017, OG Anunoby signed his rookie scale contract with the Toronto Raptors.
On 14 November 2017, OG Anunoby made his first career start against the Houston Rockets.
OG Anunoby finished his first career start with 16 points, 2 rebounds, 1 assist, and 1 steal in 30 minutes during his first career start.
By 15 December 2017, OG Anunoby led starter rookies in offensive and defensive rating.
By 15 December 2017, OG Anunoby had the third highest true shooting percentage among rookie starters.
By 15 December 2017, OG Anunoby had the best turnover-to-assist ratio for a non-guard among rookie starters.
On 29 January 2019, OG Anunoby was named a member of the World Team representing the United Kingdom for the 2019 Rising Stars Challenge.
In April 2019, OG Anunoby had an emergency appendectomy which caused him to miss most of the Raptors' championship playoff run.
OG Anunoby dressed for the NBA Finals but did not play as the Raptors won the title in 2019.
The Raptors became the first British team to win an NBA championship with OG Anunoby on the roster.
On 1 March 2020, OG Anunoby scored 32 points and recorded seven steals along with seven rebounds and three assists against the Denver Nuggets.
On 3 September 2020, OG Anunoby hit a game-winning buzzer-beater three-pointer in Game 3 of the Eastern Conference semifinals against the Boston Celtics.
OG Anunoby finished the game with 12 points after hitting the game-winning buzzer-beater three-pointer.
The buzzer-beater prevented the Raptors from going down to a 0–3 deficit to the Celtics.
The Raptors eventually fell in seven games despite OG Anunoby's performance.
On 21 December 2020, OG Anunoby signed a four-year, $72 million extension with the Toronto Raptors through the 2024-25 season.
On 24 January 2021, OG Anunoby scored a season-high 30 points while getting eight rebounds, one assist, five steals, and a block against the Indiana Pacers.
OG Anunoby joined former Raptor Kawhi Leonard as the only players with multiple games scoring 30 points, five rebounds, and five steals in franchise history.
On 1 November 2021, OG Anunoby scored a career-high 36 points along with six rebounds and two assists against the Knicks.
On 25 February 2022, OG Anunoby was sidelined due to a right finger fracture suffered against the Charlotte Hornets.
On 3 March 2022, OG Anunoby was ruled out for two weeks to rest his fractured finger.
On 16 November 2022, OG Anunoby scored a season-high 32 points during a 112-104 win against the Miami Heat.
During the 2022-23 season, OG Anunoby led the league in steals.
OG Anunoby became the first Raptors player and first British player to lead the NBA in steals during the 2022-23 season.
At the end of the 2022-23 season, OG Anunoby was named to the NBA All-Defensive Second Team for the first time.
On 30 December 2023, OG Anunoby, along with Precious Achiuwa and Malachi Flynn, were traded to the New York Knicks in exchange for RJ Barrett, Immanuel Quickley, and a second-round pick.
On 1 January 2024, OG Anunoby made his debut as a New York Knick, putting up 17 points and six rebounds against the Minnesota Timberwolves.
During his first 10 games with the Knicks, OG Anunoby set an NBA record for a +170 plus-minus rating.
On 8 February 2024, OG Anunoby had surgery on his right elbow to remove a loose bone fragment and was sidelined for a month.
OG Anunoby returned to play against the Philadelphia 76ers on 12 March 2024 after his surgery.
On June 24, 2024, OG Anunoby declined his $19.9M player option with the Knicks, becoming a free agent.
OG Anunoby has said that inspiring kids in Great Britain to play basketball is one of his goals.
OG Anunoby is considered one of the best British players to ever play in the NBA.
In 2023, OG Anunoby became a minority stake owner of the London Lions.
